title: A Scientometric Review of Construction Health, Safety and Wellbeing: Trends, Gaps, Regulation and Organisational Structures
content: The construction industry has always been lagging behind with the development con-cerning worker health, safety and well-being due to an inherently anarchic nature and a non-conformal culture. However, less effort has been put toward reviewing these critical areas along with newly arising issues, gaps and areas of further research for its better implementation to achieve enhanced regulatory compliance. This study executed the scientometric review to gauge the level of research productivity and knowledge on Construction Industry Occupational Health Safety and Welfare between 1952 and 2025 with the help of the PRISMA research design. The efforts are concentrated through co-authorships and co-occurring keyword and co-citation analyses, as well as via cross-referencing with respective countries and years of publication, which will sketch out the key development of this discipline. Revealing critically important analysis through quantitative methods of scientometric mapping for several bibliographic rec-ords, 878 extracted from the Scopus database. Nonetheless, the Safety Science journal has been the main repository of publications. The study intended to share a broad exami-nation of the environmental exposure scenario and preliminary advancements on health and safety practices in the construction industry. New linkages and future trends in construction-related occupation were alluded to in this research. This work serves a significant reference of good intellectual intervention direction and policy to improve worker safety and health in the construction industry. The study also came up with a proposed framework on occupational health, safety, and wellbeing within the con-struction industry and focused on compliance with regulations and organizational structures.
